policy_context.execution_authorization_reference: Current explicit owner instruction 2026-10-22 authorizes bounded exploratory M4 measurements and remeasurement after material instrumentation changes, using fresh operation IDs and full containment; no retry after a gate failure and no hard-gate bypass.
policy_context.resource_basis: A single bounded, two-arm exploratory test of the opt-in M4 Upsert group-commit prototype versus ordinary per-call Upsert. Both arms use identical 1,024-document seeds, four concurrent writers × eight independent Upsert calls, two concurrent search readers, one default compaction, explicit flush, reopen verification, WAL fsync enabled, and unchanged containment/resource caps. Group commit coalesces only overlapping calls for at most 500 us or four records, persists them using existing atomic ApplyBatch WAL/replay semantics, then publishes the group atomically; this remains linearizable for overlapping calls but may add bounded queue delay. Record end-to-end per-call latency, pre-dispatch group-formation wait, per-call batch-size evidence (require at least one multi-record group), reader latency, WAL fsync counts, and durability/reopen checks; do not compare against the older ApplyBatch API arm as identical call semantics. One operation only; any preflight/runtime/containment failure consumes it and is not retried. Exploratory evidence, not qualification or production authorization.
policy_context.risk_acceptance_reference: The standard contention profile is four-arm; writer_group_commit is a separate two-arm per-call Upsert experiment. All are descriptive only: shared-host pressure, one round per arm and test-scale workloads prohibit causal, qualification or architecture-win claims. ApplyBatch and Upsert call latencies have different units and must not be compared as equivalent tail samples.
